purpose: Verify full-factory one-hour C execution using the same constructive candidate tool as A, with model-selected tools and explicit candidate application.
initialization: Original cold WIP and common time-zero releases; not steady state. Old C failure remains immutable; this is a declared new controller development variant, not a reset or continuation of its spent budget.
execution: Serial after B recovery terminates. Preserve evaluated-model isolation and freeze every executed source/configuration/input/dependency file before calls.
decision_ownership: C chooses read_page, solve method and parameters, observes actual candidate feedback, then explicitly applies a valid candidate. No automatic application, correction of choices or default production dispatch.
constructor_accounting: The shared deterministic constructor requests zero CP seconds. Its calls, actual elapsed time, failures, candidate identity and unfinished reservations are separately recorded and included in end-to-end cost. The construction time limit is a soft algorithm limit, not a claim that the entire tool invocation cannot exceed it.
stopping: Stop and preserve all evidence on transport failure, invalid action or explicit apply, resource exhaustion, pending resource ambiguity, or audit failure. No automatic new run ID or replay of completed calls. Exhausted CP allocation disables CP actions but leaves separately accounted constructive/read/apply actions available.
acceptance: A complete 3600-second trace, independent physical/source/opportunity audit, model-to-tool-to-candidate-to-apply attribution and full ledger reconciliation are all required. Partial execution or a successful mock test is not a passing one-hour C gate.
comparison_boundary: Development execution/cost evidence only. The shared CP allocation is comparable with the registered A one-hour development ceiling; differing actual model, constructor, simulation and audit costs remain visible. No formal quality ranking or claim of online production benefit.
